articles.headline: Structure First: The Inverted Pyramid and Visual Organization
articles.blurb: The inverted pyramid makes web content easier to consume by putting the essential message first and progressively adding supporting detail, ensuring readers understand the key point even if they stop early. Individual paragraphs should similarly lead with their main idea, while descriptive headings, short paragraphs, lists, and selective emphasis provide visual entry points for people scanning rather than reading linearly. A useful test is whether someone can understand something meaningful from a page within five seconds without reading its body copy. AI-generated writing is particularly worth checking for conclusions buried beneath unnecessary setup.

articles.headline: Web Environment Integrity vs. Private Access Tokens - They're the same thing!
articles.blurb: Web Environment Integrity (WEI) and Apple's Private Access Tokens (PAT) both use signed browser or device attestations. A site can request proof that a visitor uses a genuine, non-jailbroken iPhone with Safari, then reject Firefox on Linux. WEI can additionally bind an attestation to a specific operation. The two proposals differ mainly in presentation: PAT is framed around fewer CAPTCHAs, while WEI is framed around service-provider verification.

articles.headline: PwnEscape: Guest-to-Host KVM Escape (CVE-2026-99999)
articles.blurb: Researchers found a Linux networking flaw that lets an untrusted VM guest alter IPv4 header bytes after the host kernel validates them. Guest-controlled checksum metadata can change the IPv4 header length, causing the kernel to copy 32 bytes beyond the packet's logical data and transmit them as apparent IP options. In a controlled KVM lab, the disclosure supported selected 64-byte host-kernel writes and execution of a host-root helper. The upstream fix, commit 6785011f8b16, validates checksum_start before checksum completion across five IPv4 consumers.

Tactical vulnerabilities represent exploit chains that chain together smaller severity issues for a larger impact and require exploit verification in a staging environment.

articles.blurb: Representatives from Anthropic have quietly pitched a draft AI safety bill to lawmakers. Under the bill, the government could only block a model's release or use if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk of more than $1B in damages, or of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people via the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developers' controls, or a cyberattack. articles.blurb: Accenture has hired JPMorgan to explore the sale of its Greater China consulting operations in a deal potentially worth up to $1.5 billion. articles.headline: Microsoft exits UK data center deal amid power delays
articles.blurb: Microsoft reportedly terminated its agreement for capacity at Nscale's planned Loughton facility amid electricity supply delays that could extend into the 2030s. Nscale says the development will proceed and its other Microsoft contracts remain unaffected, highlighting the growing importance of power availability in AI infrastructure planning.

articles.headline: Enterprise AI outcomes depend on the art of unlearning
articles.blurb: Enterprise AI adoption often falls short because organizations overlook the human element of change management. Successful digital transformation in the agentic era requires empowering employees to unlearn old software habits, supported by dedicated roles like Forward Deployed Engineers and Agentic Design Leads.

articles.headline: Enterprise AI needs runtime governance and better context
articles.blurb: Scaling enterprise AI requires coordinating what agents know with what they are permitted to do. Runtime access controls, audit trails, retrieval, and memory need to work together as agents operate across enterprise systems.

articles.headline: The agents nobody meant to build
articles.blurb: IT leaders face an emerging challenge with unsanctioned AI agents created inadvertently by employees using approved desktop tools and recurring workflows. Gartner forecasts that 40% of enterprises will demote or shut down agents by 2027 due to governance gaps, security risks, and a lack of ownership visibility. Managing this risk requires placing hard limits on what agents can touch and integrating education directly into tool access.

articles.headline: Cloudflare expands enterprise integrations for its AI workspace
articles.blurb: Cloudflare expanded the partner ecosystem for Cloudflare OS with integrations spanning Asana, Box, Canva, ClickHouse, GitHub, Gong, and Notion. articles.headline: Lenovo's AI Express targets enterprises waiting for AI servers
articles.blurb: Lenovo's AI Express is a quick-ship programme developed with Nvidia that aims to cut enterprise AI server lead times to as little as 15 business days. The offering provides three pre-validated configurations ranging from small inference setups to large generative AI platforms using Blackwell hardware. articles.headline: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Exploited Again
articles.blurb: Cisco confirmed that a zero-day vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 with a CVSS score of 9.8, is actively being exploited in the wild. Security agencies, including CISA and Germany's BSI, have issued warnings and urgent patching deadlines.

articles.headline: Why GPU Cloud Observability Is Harder Than It Looks
articles.blurb: GPU cloud observability requires connecting physical infrastructure topology with active workloads, yet traditional monitoring tools often remain isolated by subsystem. articles.headline: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site

articles.headline: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws

articles.blurb: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. articles.headline: Dutch Police Arrest ‘Reformed’ Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
articles.blurb: Authorities in the Netherlands have arrested a 23-year-old convicted cybercriminal on suspicion of aiding in data thefts and extortions by the prolific hacker group ShinyHunters. articles.headline: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
articles.blurb: A U.S. Army soldier who pleaded guilty to hacking into multiple telecommunications companies and stealing mobile call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers in 2024 was sentenced to 70 months in federal prison today and ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution to victims.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
articles.blurb: The consumer data broker Radaris.com has long had a reputation for ignoring requests to remove personal information from its vast empire of people-search services online. That reputation caught up with the company recently in a lawsuit alleging Radaris violated a New Jersey privacy law that provides for hefty fines against data brokers that publish personal information on state law enforcement officials. In the face of repeated stonewalling and prevarication by attorneys for Radaris, the judge in the case ordered that radaris.com and more than a dozen other data broker domains be transferred to the plaintiffs.

articles.headline: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses

Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.blurb: Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook. articles.headline: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan
articles.blurb: DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday. Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.

articles.headline: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult

articles.headline: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods

However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.
